sections.content:
23,770 people

were counted on the census as "pharmaceutical technicians" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Pharmaceutical technicians work in hospitals or in the community and assist pharmacists in the preparation and dispensing of drugs and medicines.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "pharmaceutical technicians" there were more women than men (84.2% compared with 15.8%).

This means "pharmaceutical technicians" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health and social care associate professionals".

Men made up 15.8% and women made up 84.2% of "pharmaceutical technicians"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "pharmaceutical technicians" included:

  • senior care workers
  • primary education teaching professionals
  • company secretaries and administrators

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "pharmaceutical technicians" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "pharmaceutical technicians", 15.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "pharmaceutical technicians" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "pharmaceutical technicians" included:

  • elementary storage supervisors
  • office supervisors
  • midwifery nurses

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "pharmaceutical technicians" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "pharmaceutical technicians" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "pharmaceutical technicians", 10.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (66.5% compared with 33.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (98.5%) than self-employed (1.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
